'''Aaron Jarrell Hammons''' (born August 27, 1992) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue Boilermakers]] before being drafted by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] with the 46th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].

==High school career==
Hammons first attended [[Carmel High School (Carmel, Indiana)|Carmel High School]] in Indiana, where he averaged 8.3 points and 7.8 rebounds as a sophomore, earning honorable mention Associated Press accolades. In his junior season, he transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]], where as a senior, he averaged 7.0 points, 6.8 rebounds and 4.0 blocks per game.<ref name="Bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/aj_hammons_801820.html|title=A.J. Hammons Bio|work=PurdueSports.com|access-date=December 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160707050444/http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/aj_hammons_801820.html|archive-date=July 7, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

When he graduated, he was given a four-star rating by Scout.com<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/player/126296-a-j-hammons|title=A.J. Hammons – Scout.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161221003236/http://www.scout.com/player/126296-a-j-hammons|work=Scout.com|access-date=December 5, 2016|archive-date=December 21, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and by Rivals.com.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/10350|title=A.J. Hammons – Rivals.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220819083234/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/10350|work=Rivals.com|access-date=December 5, 2016|archive-date=August 19, 2022|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Hammons was named to the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] All-Freshman Team at the conclusion of his first season playing for the [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue Boilermakers]], where he averaged 10.6 points, 6.0 rebounds and 2.0 blocks per game.<ref name="Bio" /> At the conclusion of his sophomore season, Hammons had an average of 10.8 points, 7.4 rebounds and 3.1 blocks per game. He was awarded honorable mention [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] as well as being named to the Big Ten All-Defensive Team. He was named second-team All-Big Ten as a junior and was again awarded a spot on the Big Ten All-Defensive Team.<ref name="Bio" />

In his senior season, Hammons averaged 15.0 points, 8.2 rebounds, 2.5 blocks and 1.1 assists while shooting .592 from the floor.<ref name="Signed">{{cite web|first=Arya|last=Ahmadi|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-aj-hammons/|title=Mavs sign A.J. Hammons|work=Mavs.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818173938/http://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-aj-hammons/|archive-date=August 18, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> That season, he was named the 2016 Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year, first-team All-Big Ten, and was again named to the Big Ten All-Defensive Team. He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]]<ref>{{cite web|last=Payne|first=Terrence|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|work=FoxSports.com|date=February 11, 2016|access-date=February 19, 2016}}</ref> and was named one of the five finalists for the [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Award]].

==Professional career==

===Dallas Mavericks (2016–2017)===
On June 23, 2016, Hammons was selected by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] with the 46th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com.au/nba/draft2016/story/_/id/16400858/2016-nba-draft-dallas-mavericks-draft-aj-hammons-purdue-center-no-46-overall|title=Mavericks draft A.J. Hammons, Purdue center, at No. 46 overall|work=ESPN.com|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=June 23, 2016}}</ref> On July 8, 2016, he signed with the Mavericks and joined the team for the [[2016 NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]].<ref name="Signed" /> During his rookie season, he had multiple [[assignment (NBA D-League)|assignments]] with the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 5, 2016|archive-date=September 6, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906020056/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also had three 9-point efforts with the Mavericks during the season, to go with a season-best 7 rebounds on April 7, 2017, against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hammoaj01/gamelog/2017/|title=A.J. Hammons 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=July 6, 2017}}</ref>

===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2017–2018)===
On July 7, 2017, Hammons was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in exchange for [[Josh McRoberts]], a 2023 second-round draft pick, and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-trade-josh-mcroberts|title=HEAT Trade Josh McRoberts|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=July 7, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-trade-j-hammons-miami-josh-mcroberts/|title=Mavericks trade A.J. Hammons to Miami for Josh McRoberts|work=Mavs.com|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=July 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180102012856/https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-trade-j-hammons-miami-josh-mcroberts/|archive-date=January 2, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> Hammons was waived by the Heat on February 8, 2018, without appearing in a game for the team, instead spending the majority of his tenure on assignment with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-dwyane-wade|title=HEAT Acquire Dwyane Wade Miami waives center AJ Hammons|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018}}</ref>
